Hi Emma / Ryan —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion on Acme's inference needs and the latency/cost targets for your embedding+RAG pipeline. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Key needs we heard: 100ms p95 for short-form chat (<=512 tokens), batch inference for bulk embedding generation (10k requests/day), and tighter cost visibility for token-level unit economics.
- Technical asks from the call: run a 1k-concurrent request stress test measuring p50/p95/p99 and end-to-end throughput for your typical prompt mix; measure per-1M token cost across our hosted API vs your current hyperscaler baseline; and validate KV/prefix cache hit rates with your prompt prefixes (we'll run a synthetic prefix workload you provide).

What we'll deliver this week (by EOD Monday PT):
1) A short TCO spreadsheet with per-1M token math for the model variants we discussed (gptx-small / gptx-medium and our 8-bit quantized variants).
2) A recommended test matrix (latency/throughput/cache) and a runnable script we can use with your test keys.
3) A short note on differentiators vs hyperscalers: routing/fallbacks, automatic KV prefix caching, and our dedicated capacity option for predictable tail latency.

Please confirm the test windows that work for you (we suggest Mon or Tue next week 9\u201311am PT) and attach a small sample of your prompt set (10\u201320 prompts) so we can seed the cache.

Attaching the preliminary TCO workbook and proposed test matrix for visibility.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao

Emma — thanks, confirmed for Mon 23 Mar 9am PT. We got your prompt samples (thanks). A quick preview of the items we attached and what to expect in the runs: 

- TCO workbook (redwood_tco_1M_tokens.xlsx): shows per-1M token math for the three model variants, with columns for: raw token cost (hosted list), expected committed price (assumes 30% commit discount), effective tokens/sec assumptions, and an adjusted per-1M token cost after factoring in cache hit rate. We include two cache-hit scenarios: 20% hit and 50% hit.
- Key callouts vs hyperscalers (short): hyperscaler endpoints give broad managed infra but typically charge for endpoint uptime and don't provide the same native KV/prefix caching or routing fallback we have; dedicated pools on hyperscalers can be more expensive at similar throughput once you factor in cold-starts and multi-region failover.
- Test matrix (redwood_test_matrix.csv): will run three passes per model variant: (A) baseline (cache off, single connection), (B) KV/prefix cache enabled (simulate 40% repeated prefixes), (C) aggressive prefix-dedupe (simulate 60% repetition). Each pass reports p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens consumed, and throughput.

Proposed success criteria for Acme: p95 <120ms for <=512 tokens in baseline; delta in per-1M token cost >=20% vs current hyperscaler in cache-enabled scenario to justify moving to Redwood Dedicated.

We will run the tests in the window and share raw logs + summarized results within 24 hours after the run. Marcus (cc) will own the test execution and will share the detailed test plan + script.

Best,
Aditya

Quick note — test matrix and script are attached (redwood_test_matrix.csv). High-level plan Marcus will run during Mon 9\u201311am PT: 

1) Warm-up: 5m low-rate traffic to stabilize kernels and KV cache.
2) Baseline run (A): 10m at 200 QPS, cache off, collect p50/p95/p99, and tokens consumed.
3) Cache run (B): 10m at 200 QPS, KV/prefix cache on with your prompt prefixes, capture hit-rate (expect ~40%).
4) Aggressive dedupe (C): 10m at 200 QPS, synthetic higher repetition (expect ~60% hit).
5) Embeddings batch test: single-job 10k requests, measure throughput and average tokens per request.

I added expected outputs in the CSV and a small column that converts measured hit-rate into effective % token savings and adjusted per-1M token cost. We'll drop the summarized results into the linked Google Doc and ping Emma when done.

If they want committed pricing sims for Dedicated, I'll run a quick model of 6/12 month commit tiers and share by EOD Tuesday.
